stem: The foundational text governing classical Indian theatre is the __________.
solution: The Natya Shastra of Bharata is the foundational treatise on Indian theatre.

stem: The Sanskrit play 'Abhijnanasakuntalam' was written by __________.
solution: Kalidasa wrote Abhijnanasakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala).

stem: The Sanskrit play 'Mrichchhakatika' (The Little Clay Cart) was written by __________.
solution: Mrichchhakatika was written by Shudraka.

stem: The Sanskrit political drama 'Mudrarakshasa' was written by __________.
solution: Mudrarakshasa (about Chanakya) was written by Vishakhadatta.

stem: The plays 'Ratnavali' and 'Nagananda' are attributed to king __________.
solution: The plays Ratnavali and Nagananda are attributed to Harshavardhana.

stem: The oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre tradition, still performed in Kerala, is __________.
solution: Koodiyattam of Kerala is the oldest living Sanskrit theatre tradition.

stem: Koodiyattam has been recognised by UNESCO as a __________.
solution: Koodiyattam is a UNESCO-recognised Intangible Cultural Heritage of humanity.

stem: The traditional folk theatre 'Jatra' belongs to the region of __________.
solution: Jatra is a popular folk theatre of Bengal (and eastern India).

stem: The folk theatre 'Tamasha' belongs to the state of __________.
solution: Tamasha is a folk theatre form of Maharashtra.

stem: The North Indian folk theatre 'Nautanki' is popular in __________.
solution: Nautanki is a folk theatre of Uttar Pradesh and North India.

stem: The traditional folk theatre of Gujarat is __________.
solution: Bhavai is the traditional folk theatre of Gujarat.

stem: The folk theatre 'Swang' is associated with __________.
solution: Swang is a folk theatre form of Haryana (and Punjab).

stem: The satirical folk theatre 'Bhand Pather' belongs to __________.
solution: Bhand Pather is a traditional folk theatre of Kashmir.

stem: The theatrical performance of the Ramayana known as 'Ramlila' is on the UNESCO list of __________.
solution: Ramlila is inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

stem: The Assamese one-act plays introduced by Sankardeva, performed in Sattras, are called __________.
solution: Sankardeva created the Ankia Naat plays, performed as Bhaona in Assam's Sattras.

stem: The ritual theatre 'Mudiyettu' of Kerala is on the UNESCO list of __________.
solution: Mudiyettu, a ritual theatre of Kerala, is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The folk theatre 'Therukoothu' (street play) belongs to __________.
solution: Therukoothu is a street-theatre form of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The storytelling folk form 'Burrakatha' belongs to __________.
solution: Burrakatha is a narrative folk performance of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

stem: The 'bow song' narrative form 'Villu Paatu' belongs to __________.
solution: Villu Paatu (bow song) is a musical storytelling form of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The ritual theatre 'Ramman' of the Garhwal Himalayas (a UNESCO ICH) belongs to __________.
solution: Ramman is a UNESCO-listed ritual theatre of Uttarakhand.

stem: The Konkan/Goa folk theatre depicting the ten incarnations of Vishnu is __________.
solution: Dashavatar is a folk theatre of the Konkan (Goa/Maharashtra) region.

stem: The folk theatre 'Maach' belongs to the state of __________.
solution: Maach is a folk theatre of Madhya Pradesh.

stem: The National School of Drama, India's premier theatre institution, is located in __________.
solution: The National School of Drama (NSD) is in New Delhi.

stem: The National School of Drama was established in the year __________.
solution: The National School of Drama was established in 1959.

stem: The influential director who shaped the National School of Drama was __________.
solution: Ebrahim Alkazi was a legendary director and head of the National School of Drama.

stem: The playwright who wrote 'Tughlaq' and 'Hayavadana' was __________.
solution: Girish Karnad wrote Tughlaq and Hayavadana.

stem: The Marathi playwright who wrote 'Ghashiram Kotwal' and 'Sakharam Binder' was __________.
solution: Vijay Tendulkar wrote Ghashiram Kotwal and Sakharam Binder.

stem: The theatre director who founded 'Naya Theatre' and created 'Charandas Chor' was __________.
solution: Habib Tanvir founded Naya Theatre and directed Charandas Chor, blending folk traditions.

stem: The Bengali director who pioneered 'Third Theatre' and street theatre was __________.
solution: Badal Sircar pioneered the 'Third Theatre' and street theatre movement.

stem: The cultural wing of the leftist movement that shaped modern Indian theatre was the __________.
solution: The Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA), formed in 1943, shaped modern Indian theatre.

stem: The commercial theatre tradition that flourished in 19th-century Bombay with proscenium staging was the __________ theatre.
solution: Parsi theatre was a popular commercial urban theatre of 19th-century Bombay.

stem: The Hindi playwright who wrote 'Ashadh Ka Ek Din' was __________.
solution: Mohan Rakesh wrote the landmark Hindi play Ashadh Ka Ek Din.

stem: In Sanskrit drama, the comic character (companion of the hero) is the __________.
solution: The Vidushaka is the comic companion character in Sanskrit drama.

stem: In Sanskrit theatre, the stage manager/narrator who begins the play is the __________.
solution: The Sutradhara is the stage manager/narrator who introduces the play.

stem: The playwright Bhasa is known for early Sanskrit plays such as __________.
solution: Bhasa wrote early Sanskrit plays like Swapnavasavadatta.

stem: The Kerala temple theatre depicting the story of Krishna is __________.
solution: Krishnattam is a Kerala temple dance-drama depicting the life of Krishna.

stem: The playwright Bhavabhuti is famous for the Sanskrit play __________.
solution: Bhavabhuti wrote Uttararamacharita.

stem: The traditional 'Ram Lila' is enacted especially during the festival of __________.
solution: Ramlila is enacted during the Dussehra/Navratri season, culminating in Vijayadashami.

stem: The dramatic performances in temples of a purely religious character are called __________ theatre.
solution: Temple performances of religious character are a form of ritual theatre.

stem: The three types of Indian theatre are broadly classical (Sanskrit), traditional/folk and __________.
solution: Indian theatre is broadly classical, folk/traditional and modern.

stem: The father of the modern Indian (Hindi) film-theatre stage, who founded Prithvi Theatres, was __________.
solution: Prithviraj Kapoor founded Prithvi Theatres, a landmark in modern Indian theatre.

stem: The traditional folk theatre 'Powada' from Maharashtra is a form of __________.
solution: Powada is a heroic ballad performance form of Maharashtra.

stem: The mask theatre 'Chho/Chhau' combines dance and __________.
solution: Chhau combines dance, martial movement and dramatic storytelling.

stem: In Sanskrit drama, the concept that a play should end __________ was a key convention.
solution: Classical Sanskrit drama conventionally avoided depicting tragedy/death on stage and ended happily.

stem: The play 'Charandas Chor' by Habib Tanvir used the folk traditions of __________.
solution: Habib Tanvir's Charandas Chor drew on the Chhattisgarhi Nacha folk tradition.

stem: The main aim of the IPTA was to use theatre for __________.
solution: The IPTA used theatre for social and political awakening.

stem: The Kerala ritual dance-drama 'Theyyam' combines worship with __________.
solution: Theyyam combines ritual worship with dance, music and elaborate costume and make-up.

stem: The classical Indian playwright most celebrated in world literature is __________.
solution: Kalidasa is the most celebrated Sanskrit playwright in world literature.

stem: The 'Sutradhara' literally means the __________.
options: holder of the thread (of the play)
solution: Sutradhara literally means 'holder of the thread', i.e. the one who holds the play together.

stem: Indian theatre traditions are significant because they preserve __________.
options: living oral, musical and dramatic heritage
solution: Indian theatre traditions preserve a living oral, musical and dramatic heritage.
